To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 service review

Dana, I promised last month that I would report back once my writer had been through a real trial. It has now survived eight days of a civil trial, so here is the review I owe you.

I took my Stenvale Aria 3 to Harbor Point Steno Service on Monday, October 19, and picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days against the ten quoted. The estimate was $285 for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and firmware update. The final work included full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning and an update from firmware 4.0.7 to 4.2.1.

The bill came to $310 because I also approved a $25 internal battery replacement. Gloria emailed to say the battery was holding about 60 percent of its rated capacity and specifically said she would not replace it without my approval. I appreciated being asked rather than finding the charge at pickup. I paid by card myself, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court. For the work done, I think $310 was fair. The invoice lists a 90-day warranty on the work.

The important part is how it writes. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight trial days, I am satisfied with the repair. That is not a long-term durability report, but it is a more useful test than a few practice takes at home.

Gloria also sent the machine back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from a service shop before. It gave me a clear record of what had actually been done, and I would like to see more of that.

A loaner was provided, a Stenvale Aria 2. Unfortunately, its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I reported that by email. At pickup, Gloria’s email said they would repair the tilt arm. I cannot say whether that has since been done, but it is worth checking the loaner’s support before taking it out to work.

Communication is the real weakness. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. The phone rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day about the battery; that email referred to a voicemail from her. There was email follow-through, but it does not change the fact that I could not reach the shop or leave a message when I called.

Their stated phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. For anyone working a Monday docket, that is a significant limitation, not a small inconvenience. I would arrange timing and a backup plan in advance rather than count on reaching someone by phone when a problem comes up.

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back.

Dana, based on this visit, I would trust Gloria with another Aria 3 number bar repair, and I would use Harbor Point again. The technical work earned that confidence. I would go in with clear arrangements about contact and would check any loaner carefully. Good work on the writer; a phone setup that needs attention.

Maureen
